head_coach.name: Javier Aguirre
head_coach.play_style_summary: Focusing on the philosophy of 'structure first, flexibility always', Aguirre's core system is a balanced 4-3-3 that emphasizes building from the back and maintaining midfield stability via a single pivot. Under his guidance, Mexico frequently morphs into variations such as a 3-4-2-1, 4-2-3-1, or a highly compact 4-1-4-1 mid-match to counter opposing tactics and prioritize defensive compactness.

key_players.name: Santiago Giménez
key_players.performance_stats: The 25-year-old AC Milan striker remains El Tri's premier attacking asset. Though navigating recovery from previous injury spells in Serie A, his high-volume goalscoring history (including 65 career goals for Feyenoord) secures his place as Mexico's primary offensive reference point.

key_players.name: Edson Álvarez
key_players.performance_stats: As the national team captain and Fenerbahçe anchor, the 28-year-old acts as the vital defensive pivot. He is essential in shielding the back line, regulating match tempo, and translating Aguirre's tactical requirements onto the pitch.

key_players.name: Armando González
key_players.performance_stats: Nicknamed 'La Hormiga', the 23-year-old Guadalajara sensation experienced a meteoric rise, claiming the Liga MX Clausura 2026 Player of the Tournament after tallying 24 goals over the season, which secured both his national team debut and a spot on the 2026 World Cup roster.

injuries_and_absences.absence_reason: Ruptured Achilles tendon suffered in March 2026, officially excluding him from the 2026 World Cup roster.
